symptom: PC-A in VLAN 10 cannot ping PC-B in VLAN 10 connected to Switch 2.
ai_root_cause: VLAN 10 traffic is blocked across the trunk link because Switch1 interface FastEthernet0/1 is explicitly configured to only allow VLAN 20 ('switchport trunk allowed vlan 20'), excluding VLAN 10.
ai_evidence: Switch1 running-config shows 'switchport trunk allowed vlan 20' under interface FastEthernet0/1 and show interfaces trunk confirms 'Vlans allowed on trunk: 20'.
ai_fix_steps: Log into Switch1 and enter interface configuration mode: 'interface FastEthernet0/1'; Add VLAN 10 to the trunk allowed list: 'switchport trunk allowed vlan add 10'; Verify allowed VLANs on trunk: 'show interfaces trunk'

symptom: PC-1 in VLAN 20 is unable to obtain traffic or reach gateway. Switch logs report native VLAN mismatch.
ai_root_cause: Native VLAN mismatch on the trunk link connecting Switch1 and Switch2 via interface GigabitEthernet0/1. Switch1 is configured with Native VLAN 10 while Switch2 is configured with default Native VLAN 1.
ai_evidence: Switch1 Trunking Native VLAN: 10 (Sales) vs Switch2 Trunking Native VLAN: 1 (default), triggering %CDP-4-NATIVE_VLAN_MISMATCH on GigabitEthernet0/1.
ai_fix_steps: Enter Switch2 interface configuration mode: 'interface GigabitEthernet0/1'; Change native VLAN to match Switch1: 'switchport trunk native vlan 10'; Verify interface configuration: 'show interfaces Gi0/1 switchport'

symptom: PC connected to Switch1 Fa0/5 has no network access and fails all pings.
ai_root_cause: VLAN 30 is assigned to interface FastEthernet0/5 on Switch1, but VLAN 30 has not been created in the switch VLAN database (missing from 'show vlan brief'), preventing traffic forwarding on that port.
ai_evidence: show interface Fa0/5 status lists Vlan 30, but VLAN 30 is absent from show vlan brief output.
ai_fix_steps: Enter Switch1 global configuration mode: 'configure terminal'; Create missing VLAN 30: 'vlan 30'; Exit configuration mode and verify creation: 'show vlan brief'

symptom: PC-2 attached to Fa0/10 cannot reach default gateway 192.168.1.1.
ai_root_cause: Switch1 interface FastEthernet0/10 is configured in default Access VLAN 1 instead of VLAN 10, isolating host PC-2 from the VLAN 10 gateway network.
ai_evidence: Access Mode VLAN: 1 (default)
ai_fix_steps: Enter Switch1 interface configuration mode: 'interface FastEthernet0/10'; Assign port to VLAN 10: 'switchport access vlan 10'; Verify VLAN assignment: 'show interfaces Fa0/10 switchport'

symptom: Trunk port between Switch1 and Switch2 is down, disabling inter-switch traffic.
ai_root_cause: Both Switch1 and Switch2 interface Gi0/2 are configured with DTP Administrative Mode 'dynamic auto'. DTP auto-to-auto negotiation cannot initiate trunking, causing both ports to default to Operational Mode 'static access'.
ai_evidence: Switch1 and Switch2 both report 'Administrative Mode: dynamic auto' and 'Operational Mode: static access' on interface Gi0/2
ai_fix_steps: Enter interface mode on Switch1: 'interface GigabitEthernet0/2'; Configure static trunk mode: 'switchport mode trunk'; Enter interface mode on Switch2: 'interface GigabitEthernet0/2'; Configure static trunk mode: 'switchport mode trunk'; Verify trunk operation: 'show interfaces Gi0/2 trunk'

symptom: PC-A experiences intermittent loss of connectivity and duplicate IP warnings.
ai_root_cause: IP address conflict on the local network segment. Both PC-A and PC-B are configured with the identical IP address (192.168.1.100), causing ARP cache flapping on Router1 and network disruption.
ai_evidence: PC-A and PC-B Host IP Config both show IP Address: 192.168.1.100, and Router1 show ip arp binds 192.168.1.100 to two different MAC addresses (0001.AAAA.1111 and 0002.BBBB.2222).
ai_fix_steps: Reconfigure PC-B (or PC-A) with a unique, unassigned IP address on the 192.168.1.0/24 subnet (or set to dynamic DHCP assignment); Clear the stale ARP table entries on Router1 using the CLI command: 'clear ip arp 192.168.1.100'

symptom: PC-1 can reach local subnet hosts (10.0.1.0/24) but cannot reach remote servers (10.0.2.10).
ai_root_cause: PC-1 is configured with an incorrect default gateway IP address (10.0.1.254). The actual gateway interface on Router1 (GigabitEthernet0/0) is configured with IP address 10.0.1.1, preventing PC-1 from routing traffic outside its local subnet.
ai_evidence: PC-1 Default Gateway is 10.0.1.254, but Router1 GigabitEthernet0/0 IP address is 10.0.1.1
ai_fix_steps: Change the Default Gateway configuration on PC-1 to 10.0.1.1; Test remote connectivity from PC-1 using command: 'ping 10.0.2.10'

symptom: Host PC-3 (172.16.10.50) cannot ping Gateway 172.16.10.1.
ai_root_cause: Subnet mask mismatch between host PC-3 and Router interface GigabitEthernet0/0. PC-3 is configured with a /16 subnet mask (255.255.0.0), whereas the router interface is configured for a /24 subnet mask (255.255.255.0).
ai_evidence: PC-3 ipconfig shows 'Subnet Mask: 255.255.0.0' while Router GigabitEthernet0/0 shows 'Internet Address is 172.16.10.1/24'
ai_fix_steps: Reconfigure host PC-3 IPv4 adapter settings to set the Subnet Mask to 255.255.255.0; Verify connectivity by issuing 'ping 172.16.10.1' from PC-3

symptom: Hosts on LAN failover fail when primary router R1 goes down.
ai_root_cause: HSRP group number mismatch between R1 and R2 on interface Gi0/0. R1 is configured for HSRP group 1 while R2 is configured for group 2, preventing them from exchanging HSRP hellos and forming an Active/Standby redundancy pair.
ai_evidence: R1 show standby brief output shows 'Grp 1' while R2 show standby brief output shows 'Grp 2' with Standby state listed as 'unknown'.
ai_fix_steps: Log into R2 and enter interface configuration mode: 'interface GigabitEthernet0/0'; Remove the mismatched HSRP group configuration: 'no standby 2 ip 192.168.1.1'; Configure matching HSRP group 1: 'standby 1 ip 192.168.1.1'

symptom: Branch office PCs receive APIPA IP addresses (169.254.x.x) and cannot access company network.
ai_root_cause: Branch Router interface GigabitEthernet0/0 is missing the 'ip helper-address' configuration. Without a DHCP relay agent, broadcast DHCP requests from branch clients are dropped by the router and cannot reach the HQ Central DHCP Server (10.1.1.100), causing clients to fail DHCP discovery and assign APIPA addresses.
ai_evidence: show running-config interface Gi0/0 lacks 'ip helper-address 10.1.1.100'
ai_fix_steps: Log into Branch Router global configuration mode and enter interface mode: 'interface GigabitEthernet0/0'; Configure the DHCP relay address: 'ip helper-address 10.1.1.100'; On Branch PC, execute 'ipconfig /renew' to obtain a valid IP address from HQ DHCP server

symptom: New PCs added to Sales department fail to obtain IP address from Router DHCP pool.
ai_root_cause: The DHCP pool SALES_POOL on Router1 is completely exhausted (100% utilization with 254 out of 254 addresses leased or bound), leaving no available IP addresses to allocate to new PCs in the Sales department.
ai_evidence: show ip dhcp pool SALES_POOL indicates 'Utilization mark (high/low) : 100 / 0' and 'Total leased addresses : 254'
ai_fix_steps: Clear inactive or stale DHCP bindings: 'clear ip dhcp binding *'; Expand the DHCP pool subnet size (e.g., change subnet mask from /24 to /23) or shorten the DHCP lease time to allow address reuse

symptom: Router interface IP conflicts with newly connected host PC.
ai_root_cause: The DHCP server configuration lacks an excluded address rule for the router's interface IP (192.168.1.1). Because 192.168.1.1 is within the configured network pool 192.168.1.0/24 and not excluded, the DHCP server assigned 192.168.1.1 to a newly connected client host.
ai_evidence: ip dhcp pool LAN_POOL defines network 192.168.1.0 255.255.255.0 without a corresponding global 'ip dhcp excluded-address 192.168.1.1' command.
ai_fix_steps: Enter Router global configuration mode: 'configure terminal'; Exclude the gateway IP address from being assigned by DHCP: 'ip dhcp excluded-address 192.168.1.1'; Clear active DHCP bindings to remove the duplicate lease: 'clear ip dhcp binding *'

symptom: PCs in VLAN 40 receive IP addresses in 192.168.20.0/24 range instead of 192.168.40.0/24.
ai_root_cause: The DHCP pool 'VLAN40' has an incorrect network statement configured as 192.168.20.0/24 instead of 192.168.40.0/24, causing the router to distribute IP addresses from the wrong subnet to VLAN 40 clients.
ai_evidence: ip dhcp pool VLAN40 network 192.168.20.0 255.255.255.0
ai_fix_steps: Enter DHCP pool configuration mode on Router: 'ip dhcp pool VLAN40'; Remove incorrect network statement: 'no network 192.168.20.0 255.255.255.0'; Configure correct network statement: 'network 192.168.40.0 255.255.255.0'; Verify with: 'show running-config | section dhcp'

symptom: PC can ping 8.8.8.8 directly, but browsing to www.cisco.com fails with domain name resolution error.
ai_root_cause: The Host PC is configured with an incorrect DNS server address (192.168.1.254). According to topology notes, the correct internal DNS server is 10.0.0.53, causing DNS resolution requests to time out.
ai_evidence: Host PC ipconfig /all shows 'DNS Servers . . . . . . . . . . . : 192.168.1.254' and nslookup reports 'Connection to 192.168.1.254 timed out'.
ai_fix_steps: Step 1: On Host PC, change the IPv4 DNS server configuration from 192.168.1.254 to 10.0.0.53 (or update the DHCP pool option 'dns-server 10.0.0.53' on Router1 if IP settings are dynamically assigned).; Step 2: Flush DNS cache on Host PC using 'ipconfig /flushdns'.; Step 3: Verify hostname resolution by executing 'nslookup www.cisco.com'.

symptom: Pinging server by FQDN 'server1.company.local' succeeds, but pinging short name 'server1' fails.
ai_root_cause: The Primary DNS Suffix is not configured on PC-Client. When querying single-label hostnames like 'server1', the operating system requires a primary DNS suffix or DNS suffix search list (such as 'company.local') to automatically append and perform FQDN resolution.
ai_evidence: Primary DnS Suffix . . . . . . . . . . . : is blank in ipconfig /all output
ai_fix_steps: Configure Primary DNS Suffix on PC-Client via System Properties -> Computer Name -> Change -> More -> Primary DNS suffix of this computer: 'company.local'; Alternatively, configure DHCP Option 015 (DNS Domain Name) on the network DHCP server to distribute 'company.local' automatically; Verify resolution by running 'ping server1' or 'nslookup server1' from the client command prompt

symptom: DNS queries sent to corporate DNS server 172.16.50.2 time out across the router.
ai_root_cause: Access list DMZ_IN permits only TCP port 53 traffic to DNS server 172.16.50.2, but standard DNS client requests use UDP port 53. Consequently, UDP DNS queries from VLAN 10 are blocked and dropped by sequence 20 (deny ip any any).
ai_fix_steps: Enter router access-list configuration mode: 'ip access-list extended DMZ_IN'; Add permit rule for UDP DNS traffic: '15 permit udp 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 host 172.16.50.2 eq 53'

symptom: PC-A (192.168.10.10) gets IP and ping gateway works, but cannot reach Server in VLAN 30 (10.0.30.50).
ai_root_cause: Router1 routing table lacks a route to the destination network 10.0.30.0/24 and has no gateway of last resort configured, preventing traffic destined for 10.0.30.50 from being routed.
ai_evidence: Router1 show ip route shows 'Gateway of last resort is not set' and lacks any route for 10.0.30.0/24.
ai_fix_steps: Enter Router1 global configuration mode: 'configure terminal'; Configure static route to destination subnet via Router2 next-hop IP: 'ip route 10.0.30.0 255.255.255.0 172.16.12.2'; Verify route entry: 'show ip route'

symptom: OSPF neighbor adjacency between Router1 and Router2 stays in INIT/EXSTART state.
ai_root_cause: OSPF Hello and Dead timer mismatch on interface GigabitEthernet0/1 between Router1 and Router2. OSPF requires identical Hello and Dead intervals to establish adjacency.
ai_evidence: Router1 has 'Hello 10, Dead 40' while Router2 has 'Hello 30, Dead 120'
ai_fix_steps: Enter Router2 interface configuration mode: 'interface GigabitEthernet0/1'; Adjust Hello interval to match Router1: 'ip ospf hello-interval 10'; Adjust Dead interval to match Router1: 'ip ospf dead-interval 40'; Verify OSPF neighbor reaches FULL state: 'show ip ospf neighbor'

symptom: Router2 does not form EIGRP neighbor relationship with Router1.
ai_root_cause: EIGRP Autonomous System (AS) number mismatch (AS 100 on Router1 vs AS 200 on Router2).
ai_evidence: CLI show command outputs supplied for review.
ai_fix_steps: Change Router2 EIGRP process to 'router eigrp 100'.

symptom: Router1 fails to advertise LAN routes to Router2 via OSPF.
ai_root_cause: OSPF WAN interface GigabitEthernet0/1 misconfigured as a passive-interface.
ai_evidence: CLI show command outputs supplied for review.
ai_fix_steps: Under OSPF router configuration on Router1, execute 'no passive-interface GigabitEthernet0/1'.

symptom: BGP session between HQ Router (AS 65001) and ISP Router (AS 65500) fails to establish.
ai_root_cause: HQ Router configured with wrong remote-as (65501 instead of ISP AS 65500).
ai_evidence: CLI show command outputs supplied for review.
ai_fix_steps: On HQ Router, correct neighbor definition to 'neighbor 203.0.113.2 remote-as 65500'.

symptom: PC-A (192.168.10.5) cannot access Web Server (10.0.0.100) on port 80.
ai_root_cause: ACL missing explicit 'permit ip any any' rule, causing implicit deny to block all traffic.
ai_evidence: CLI show command outputs supplied for review.
ai_fix_steps: Add rule '20 permit ip any any' to access-list BLOCK_WEB.

symptom: Host 192.168.1.50 can still SSH to Server 10.0.0.5 despite access list blocking rule.
ai_root_cause: ACL rule checks port 23 (Telnet) instead of port 22 (SSH).
ai_evidence: CLI show command outputs supplied for review.
ai_fix_steps: Replace rule 10 in SEC_ACL with 'deny tcp host 192.168.1.50 host 10.0.0.5 eq 22'.

symptom: Entire HR department (192.168.20.0/24) is blocked from accessing Internet.
ai_root_cause: Wildcard mask 0.0.0.255 matches the entire /24 subnet instead of host 192.168.20.5 (host / 0.0.0.0).
ai_evidence: CLI show command outputs supplied for review.
ai_fix_steps: Update ACL 10 rule 10 to 'deny host 192.168.20.5' or 'deny 192.168.20.5 0.0.0.0'.

symptom: Inter-departmental traffic between VLAN 10 and VLAN 20 drops at router interface.
ai_root_cause: ACL missing permit statement at end, dropping all traffic coming into Gi0/0.10.
ai_evidence: CLI show command outputs supplied for review.
ai_fix_steps: Add 'permit ip any any' to FILTER_VLAN10.

symptom: Internal LAN PCs (192.168.1.0/24) cannot reach external Internet IP addresses (8.8.8.8).
ai_root_cause: Missing 'ip nat inside' on Gi0/0 and 'ip nat outside' on Gi0/1 interface configurations.
ai_evidence: CLI show command outputs supplied for review.
ai_fix_steps: Apply 'ip nat inside' on interface Gi0/0 and 'ip nat outside' on interface Gi0/1.

symptom: LAN subnet 192.168.2.0/24 hosts cannot access Internet via NAT, while 192.168.1.0/24 works.
ai_root_cause: NAT ACL 10 does not permit the newly added subnet 192.168.2.0/24.
ai_evidence: CLI show command outputs supplied for review.
ai_fix_steps: Add line 'access-list 10 permit 192.168.2.0 0.0.0.255' to global configuration.

symptom: External clients cannot reach internal Web Server via Static NAT IP 203.0.113.50.
ai_root_cause: Static NAT configuration on the Router maps public IP 203.0.113.50 to the incorrect internal IP address 192.168.1.55 instead of the Web Server's real IP address 192.168.1.50.
ai_evidence: ip nat inside source static 192.168.1.55 203.0.113.50
ai_fix_steps: Enter Router global configuration mode; Remove incorrect static NAT mapping: 'no ip nat inside source static 192.168.1.55 203.0.113.50'; Configure correct static NAT mapping: 'ip nat inside source static 192.168.1.50 203.0.113.50'

symptom: Wireless Laptop cannot connect to Access Point; authentication fails continuously.
ai_root_cause: WPA2 pre-shared key (WPA-PSK) mismatch between the Laptop and the Access Point. The Laptop is configured with key 'SecretPass123', whereas the Access Point requires 'SecretPass123!'.
ai_evidence: Laptop Key is configured as 'SecretPass123' while AP configuration shows 'wpa-psk ascii SecretPass123!'
ai_fix_steps: On the Laptop wireless configuration settings, update the Security Key/Passphrase to 'SecretPass123!'; Alternatively, update the AP configuration under 'dot11 ssid Corporate_Wi-Fi' by entering 'wpa-psk ascii SecretPass123'

symptom: Wireless clients see SSID 'Staff_WiFi' but fail to obtain an IP address via DHCP.
ai_root_cause: VLAN 50, which is mapped to the 'Staff_WiFi' WLAN on the WLC, does not exist in Switch1's VLAN database, preventing DHCP broadcast traffic from being forwarded.
ai_evidence: Switch1 show vlan brief lists only VLAN 1 and VLAN 10; VLAN 50 is missing from the database
ai_fix_steps: Log into Switch1 global configuration mode: 'configure terminal'; Create VLAN 50: 'vlan 50'; Optionally assign a name: 'name Staff_VLAN'; Verify VLAN creation: 'show vlan brief'

symptom: Lightweight Access Point (LAP-1) remains in joining loop and fails to discover WLC.
ai_root_cause: The DHCP pool AP_POOL on the DHCP Router is missing DHCP Option 43 to supply the Wireless LAN Controller (WLC-1) management IP address (10.10.10.5) to LAP-1, causing the access point to fail CAPWAP Layer 3 discovery.
ai_evidence: LAP-1 console logs '%CAPWAP-3-ERRORLOG: Could not resolve WLC IP address via Option 43 or DNS' and 'show running-config pool AP_POOL' lacks option 43.
ai_next_command: show running-config | section ip dhcp pool AP_POOL
ai_fix_steps: Enter DHCP pool configuration mode on DHCP Router: 'ip dhcp pool AP_POOL'; Add DHCP Option 43 specifying the WLC IP address: 'option 43 ip 10.10.10.5' (or 'option 43 hex f1040a0a0a05'); Verify the DHCP pool settings: 'show running-config | section ip dhcp pool AP_POOL'

symptom: Guest Wi-Fi users can ping internal corporate server 10.0.0.100.
ai_root_cause: The router's Guest Wi-Fi gateway subinterface GigabitEthernet0/0.99 does not have an Access Control List (ACL) applied to block guest traffic from routing to the internal corporate network (10.0.0.0/8).
ai_evidence: Router show running-config interface Gi0/0.99 indicates '(No access group applied)' and Guest Laptop successfully receives ICMP replies from 10.0.0.100
ai_fix_steps: Create an extended ACL to block internal corporate subnets: 'ip access-list extended GUEST_ISOLATION'; Add rule to deny traffic to internal network: 'deny ip 192.168.99.0 0.0.0.255 10.0.0.0 0.255.255.255'; Permit all other traffic (Internet access): 'permit ip any any'; Enter subinterface mode: 'interface GigabitEthernet0/0.99'; Apply ACL inbound: 'ip access-group GUEST_ISOLATION in'; Verify guest ping to 10.0.0.100 is blocked

symptom: PC in VLAN 10 cannot access Web Server in VLAN 20. Neither VLAN can reach Internet.
ai_root_cause: Router-on-a-stick subinterfaces for VLAN 10 and VLAN 20 are missing on interface GigabitEthernet0/0, preventing inter-VLAN routing between the subnets. Additionally, no default route is configured to provide Internet reachability via GigabitEthernet0/1.
ai_evidence: show running-config interface Gi0/0 shows no subinterfaces configured and show ip route shows 'Gateway of last resort is not set' with only 203.0.113.0/30 connected
ai_fix_steps: Configure VLAN 10 subinterface: 'interface GigabitEthernet0/0.10', 'encapsulation dot1Q 10', 'ip address <VLAN10_Gateway_IP> <Subnet_Mask>'; Configure VLAN 20 subinterface: 'interface GigabitEthernet0/0.20', 'encapsulation dot1Q 20', 'ip address <VLAN20_Gateway_IP> <Subnet_Mask>'; Enable parent interface: 'interface GigabitEthernet0/0' -> 'no shutdown'; Add default route for Internet connectivity: 'ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 GigabitEthernet0/1 <Next_Hop_IP>'; Verify routing table: 'show ip route'

symptom: PC receives IP via DHCP but cannot resolve domain names or ping outside subnet.
ai_root_cause: The DHCP pool configuration on the Branch Router is handing out an incorrect default gateway and DNS server address (192.168.1.254) to clients, whereas the Branch Router's local interface Gi0/0 is configured with IP address 192.168.1.1.
ai_evidence: PC Default Gateway and DNS Server are set to 192.168.1.254, while Branch Router interface Gi0/0 has 'ip address 192.168.1.1 255.255.255.0'
ai_next_command: show running-config | section ip dhcp pool
ai_fix_steps: Enter Branch Router configuration mode and enter the DHCP pool: 'ip dhcp pool <POOL_NAME>'; Correct the default gateway: 'default-router 192.168.1.1'; Correct the DNS server: 'dns-server 192.168.1.1' (or appropriate public/internal DNS address); On the PC, refresh the DHCP lease: 'ipconfig /release' followed by 'ipconfig /renew'

symptom: Finance PC-1 (10.10.10.15) ping to Accounting Server (10.20.20.50) fails intermittently.
ai_root_cause: Switch1 interface FastEthernet0/1 is in an err-disabled (Secure-shutdown) state caused by a port security violation when unauthorized MAC address 0050.7966.9999 transmitted traffic on VLAN 10 instead of the configured MAC address 0010.a1b2.c3d4.
ai_evidence: FastEthernet0/1 is up, line protocol is down (err-disabled), Port Status: Secure-shutdown, Violation Mode: Shutdown, Configured MAC Addresses: 0010.a1b2.c3d4, Last Source Address:Vlan: 0050.7966.9999:10
ai_fix_steps: Enter Switch1 interface configuration mode: 'interface FastEthernet0/1'; If the new host is authorized, update the secure MAC address or adjust maximum allowed addresses: 'switchport port-security mac-address 0050.7966.9999' or 'switchport port-security mac-address sticky'; Recover the interface from err-disabled state: 'shutdown' followed by 'no shutdown'; Verify operational status: 'show interfaces FastEthernet0/1' and 'show port-security interface Fa0/1'
